doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His first album as a leader, Candido
summary: The first LP with Dick Katz, Whitey Mitchell, Ted Sommer, Al Cohn and Joe Puma, still used at universities.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Maestro, let's talk about your recordings as a leader. What was your first recording as a leader of the group?
And who participated in this recording? Where was it?

That was here in New York and they were jazz musicians. The pianist was . . . Dick Katz on piano. The bassist was Whitey Mitchell, on drums, Ted Sommer and Al Cohn on saxophone (also Joe Puma on guitar). That was my first recording. And after that, several recordings.
Speaking of that, Cándido? Was it mostly jazz material you recorded?
Yes, yes, on that one, yes. That recording, yes.
What type of success did it have, and . . . ?
Very good. They are still using it at the University. They use that disc to explain about jazz and Afro-Cuban rhythm.
That was . . . well, I'd estimate it was about thirty years ago - about thirty years. It was my first recording. The very first one! About thirty years ago. (Actually recorded and released in 1956)
